answer: The cedar multiplier is published, charged in marble, and trellis lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 4902 identities would post 1217 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
